design_decisions.reuse_not_reinvention: The design is NIP-0003 feature 109's: a fixture-subdirectory claim map inside tools/fixtures_self_test.sh, each subdirectory claimed by exactly one owning suite. This contract adds no second registry and no new file; NIP-0003 later registers its runtime_session row in this same array (pinned_interface.slot_rule).
design_decisions.granularity: One claim per IMMEDIATE subdirectory of tools/fixtures/. A claim covers everything below it at any depth. Claim keys containing a slash are malformed.
design_decisions.ownership_not_execution: A claim proves ownership, not execution (spec 105 text). That tools/test_convergent_review.py runs is feature 104's CI job; this feature neither runs the suite nor edits it. The claim only requires the owning suite file to exist (a regular file).
design_decisions.four_failure_modes: The spec names three: an unclaimed subdirectory, a doubly-claimed subdirectory, a claim naming a suite file that does not exist. This contract adds a FOURTH, a claim naming a subdirectory that is not on disk (a stale or mistyped row), with a fourth demonstration line `OK   claim-map   claim naming an absent subdirectory -> FAIL`. Rationale: the existing guard already fails the symmetric case (a COVERED row naming an absent fixture, "phantom"), and without it a deleted or renamed subdirectory would leave a registry row that claims nothing, undetected. Consequence, recorded in the slot rule: the NIP-0003 runtime_session row can only be added together with its directory. The three mandated lines are printed unchanged; the fourth is additive. MODE A RULING (round 1 of 105-contract, ruling on the Orchestrator's question Q1, run_state history 2026-10-09T20:28:06Z): the fourth mode is IN SCOPE because it extends the existing completeness-guard rule that a manifest row naming an absent fixture is a FAIL (source=tools/fixtures_self_test.sh section='COMPLETENESS GUARD' lines 934-937, 962-966) to claim rows; the feature text says the guard 'accounts for every file' and does not make the three named modes exhaustive.
design_decisions.positive_control: Every negative demonstration is preceded, in the same scratch tree, by proof that a COMPLETE claim map passes (rc 0, no output), and each negative must produce exactly ONE output line naming its own defect. A check that always fails, always passes, or reports the wrong defect therefore cannot satisfy a demonstration (S05 cases 12 and 13 prove it). Each printed label is also bound to its OWN failure mode: S05 cases 14-17 disable exactly one detection line of claim_map_check at a time and require that mode's OK line to disappear, its FAIL demonstration line to appear and the other three OK lines to remain.
design_decisions.map_is_consulted: The real guard calls claim_map_check on the real tree with the real array and also derives per-file accounting from the same array. S05 case 7 deletes the real row and requires the real subdirectory to become unclaimed: a map that exists but is not consulted would still pass, so the check FAILS the mutation. S05 cases 2-6 and 8-11 check each failure mode on the real script; cases 14-17 check that each demonstration label tests its own mode.
design_decisions.any_depth: The on-disk set is `find . -mindepth 1 ! -type d`. S05 cases 2-3 write a dotfile 6 path components deep inside the claimed subdirectory (counted: 147/147) and a file 6 path components deep inside an unclaimed one (named, counted /147), so a depth-limited find fails them; AT1 compares against os.walk.

reference_implementation.text:
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXTURE-SUBDIRECTORY CLAIM MAP (NDEBT-042, phase-014 feature 105; the design
# is NIP-0003 feature 109's, pulled forward -- there is no second registry).
# Every subdirectory of tools/fixtures/ is claimed by exactly one owning suite:
# one "<subdirectory>|<suite file>" row. A claim proves OWNERSHIP, not
# execution: that the owning suite runs is proven by its own CI job.
# NIP-0003's runtime_session fixtures register their row here, in the same
# change that creates that subdirectory, as:
#   "runtime_session|tools/test_runtime_session.py"
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FIXTURE_CLAIMS=(
  "convergent_review|tools/test_convergent_review.py"
)

# claim_map_check <fixtures-root> <repo-root> <claim-row>...
#
# Prints one "FAIL claim-map: ..." line per violation and returns 1 if there
# was any (0 otherwise). Violations: a malformed row; a subdirectory under
# <fixtures-root> claimed by no row; one claimed by two or more rows; a row
# naming a suite file that is not a regular file under <repo-root>; a row
# naming a subdirectory that is not on disk. Pure read: it writes nothing.
claim_map_check() {
  local fixtures_root="$1" repo_root="$2" row key suite entry bad=0
  shift 2
  local -A claim_count=()
  for row in "$@"; do
    key="${row%%|*}"; suite="${row#*|}"
    if [[ "${row}" != *"|"* || -z "${key}" || -z "${suite}" || "${key}" == */* ]]; then
      echo "FAIL claim-map: malformed claim row: ${row}"; bad=1; continue
    fi
    claim_count["${key}"]=$(( ${claim_count["${key}"]:-0} + 1 ))
    [ -f "${repo_root}/${suite}" ] || { echo "FAIL claim-map: claim for ${key} names a suite file that does not exist: ${suite}"; bad=1; }
    [ -d "${fixtures_root}/${key}" ] || { echo "FAIL claim-map: claim names a subdirectory that is not on disk: ${key}"; bad=1; }
  done
  for key in "${!claim_count[@]}"; do
    [ "${claim_count[${key}]}" -le 1 ] || { echo "FAIL claim-map: doubly-claimed subdirectory: ${key}"; bad=1; }
  done
  while IFS= read -r entry; do
    [ -n "${claim_count["${entry}"]:-}" ] || { echo "FAIL claim-map: unclaimed subdirectory: ${entry}"; bad=1; }
  done < <(cd "${fixtures_root}" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d | sed 's#^\./##' | LC_ALL=C sort)
  return "${bad}"
}

# _claim_map_case <case>: builds a private scratch tree (never under the
# repository: scratch_dirs refuses any path in or below it), proves that a
# complete claim map PASSES there (the positive control: a check that always
# fails would otherwise satisfy every negative), then breaks it in exactly one
# way and requires claim_map_check to FAIL with exactly one line naming that
# violation. Reads and writes only below ${d}.
_claim_map_case() (
  local case_name="$1" d out rc want
  local -a rows=("owned|suites/a.py")
  scratch_dirs d || return 1
  mkdir -p "${d}/fixtures/owned" "${d}/suites" || return 1
  : > "${d}/fixtures/owned/case.json"; : > "${d}/suites/a.py"; : > "${d}/suites/b.py"
  out=$(claim_map_check "${d}/fixtures" "${d}" "${rows[@]}"); rc=$?
  [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] && [ -z "${out}" ] || { echo "  control: a complete claim map must pass (rc=${rc}): ${out}"; return 1; }
  case "${case_name}" in
    unclaimed)     mkdir "${d}/fixtures/zz_unclaimed"; want="unclaimed subdirectory: zz_unclaimed" ;;
    doubly)        rows+=("owned|suites/b.py"); want="doubly-claimed subdirectory: owned" ;;
    missing-suite) rows=("owned|suites/missing.py"); want="a suite file that does not exist: suites/missing.py" ;;
    absent-subdir) rows+=("ghost|suites/a.py"); want="a subdirectory that is not on disk: ghost" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  out=$(claim_map_check "${d}/fixtures" "${d}" "${rows[@]}"); rc=$?
  [ "${rc}" -eq 1 ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] && [[ "${out}" == *"${want}"* ]] \
    || { echo "  ${case_name}: rc=${rc}: ${out}"; return 1; }
)

echo "== claim map demonstrations (guarded scratch area) =="
for _case in "unclaimed|unclaimed subdirectory" "doubly|doubly-claimed subdirectory" \
             "missing-suite|claim naming a missing suite" "absent-subdir|claim naming an absent subdirectory"; do
  if _claim_map_case "${_case%%|*}"; then
    echo "OK   claim-map   ${_case#*|} -> FAIL"
  else
    echo "FAIL claim-map   ${_case#*|}: the guard did not behave as claimed"
    fail=1
  fi
done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COMPLETENESS GUARD: every non-directory entry under tools/fixtures/, at ANY
# depth, must be accounted for: a top-level file by exactly one row above, a
# file below a subdirectory by that subdirectory's claim (FIXTURE_CLAIMS). An
# unlisted top-level file, an unclaimed or doubly-claimed subdirectory, a row
# naming an absent fixture or subdirectory, or a claim naming a missing suite
# is a FAIL.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "== completeness guard =="
ondisk=()
# find, not a glob: a glob skips dot-prefixed entries and expands a
# subdirectory to its CONTENTS (PR #31 review). -mindepth 1 ! -type d lists
# every file at every depth, dotfiles and symlinks included; the leading './'
# is stripped so top-level names match the bare basenames in COVERED. (No
# -printf: portable to non-GNU find.)
while IFS= read -r f; do ondisk+=("${f}"); done \
  < <(cd tools/fixtures && find . -mindepth 1 ! -type d | sed 's#^\./##' | LC_ALL=C sort)

claim_out=$(claim_map_check tools/fixtures "${REPO}" "${FIXTURE_CLAIMS[@]}") || {
  printf '%s\n' "${claim_out}"
  fail=1
}
declare -A claimed_dir=()
for _row in "${FIXTURE_CLAIMS[@]}"; do claimed_dir["${_row%%|*}"]=1; done
toplevel=(); nested_claimed=0; nested_unclaimed=()
for f in "${ondisk[@]}"; do
  case "${f}" in
    */*) if [ -n "${claimed_dir["${f%%/*}"]:-}" ]; then nested_claimed=$((nested_claimed + 1)); else nested_unclaimed+=("${f}"); fi ;;
    *)   toplevel+=("${f}") ;;
  esac
done
covered_sorted=()
while IFS= read -r f; do covered_sorted+=("${f}"); done \
  < <(printf '%s\n' "${COVERED[@]}" | LC_ALL=C sort -u)

unaccounted=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "${toplevel[@]}") <(printf '%s\n' "${covered_sorted[@]}"))
phantom=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "${toplevel[@]}") <(printf '%s\n' "${covered_sorted[@]}"))

if [ -n "${unaccounted}" ]; then
  echo "FAIL completeness: fixture(s) on disk not accounted for by any manifest row (dormant):"
  printf '%s\n' "${unaccounted}" | sed 's/^/       /'
  fail=1
fi
if [ "${#nested_unclaimed[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL completeness: fixture(s) below an unclaimed subdirectory (dormant):"
  printf '%s\n' "${nested_unclaimed[@]}" | sed 's/^/       /'
  fail=1
fi
if [ -n "${phantom}" ]; then
  echo "FAIL completeness: manifest row(s) name a fixture that is not on disk:"
  printf '%s\n' "${phantom}" | sed 's/^/       /'
  fail=1
fi

total=${#ondisk[@]}
accounted=$(( ${#toplevel[@]} - $(printf '%s\n' "${unaccounted}" | grep -c .) + nested_claimed ))
echo "---"
if [ "${fail}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "SELF-TEST OK: ${accounted}/${total} fixtures accounted for, 0 failed"
  exit 0
fi
echo "SELF-TEST FAILED: ${accounted}/${total} fixtures accounted for (see FAIL lines above)"
exit 1

serialization.rule: validate.sh and tools/fixtures_self_test.sh must NEVER run concurrently in the same tree, and no scratch copy of a tree may be taken while either runs in it. Reason (C13 race): the self-test copies tools/fixtures/skill_index_neg_dangling_module.json over tools/skill.json, runs validate.sh, then restores it; a concurrent validate.sh sees the dangling skill index and a concurrent scratch copy captures it. Applies to the Generator, Mode B, the Evaluator and the Orchestrator in the shared tree after promotion.
serialization.generator_discipline: Every capture is a foreground command, issued one at a time; no `&`, no run_in_background, no parallel tool calls for any command that invokes validate.sh, fixtures_self_test.sh, scratch_run.py or validator_gate.py (AT1-AT5, S05, S06, S09 and the tests inside them).
serialization.enforcement: S05, S06 and S09 start with a serial guard: it refuses (exit 4) if another process in the same working directory is running `bash tools/fixtures_self_test.sh` or `bash tools/validate.sh` (it scans /proc, excluding its own ancestors), and it takes an exclusive non-blocking flock on a lock file inside the git directory (outside the working tree), so two guarded checks cannot overlap. S05's seventeen cases run four at a time, which is safe because each case copies the real tree (which the guard has just proved idle, and which no case writes) into its own private directory and runs there against its own tools/skill.json.
serialization.limits: The verbatim acceptance-test commands cannot take the lock; for them the rule, the one-at-a-time discipline and S03 (which fails if tools/skill.json or any file outside the scope changed) are the controls. A race detected after the fact shows as an S03/S02 failure or a spurious C13 FAIL, and the affected captures are retaken in order.

containment.claim: The self-test's negative cases run in a guarded scratch area that can never touch tools/fixtures/.
containment.mechanism: (1) The cases use the existing scratch_dirs helper, which resolves the temporary root and rejects /, the repository and anything below it before creating anything. (2) _claim_map_case is a subshell function that names no repository path and roots every write at ${d}. (3) claim_map_check, which also runs on the real tree, is a pure read.
containment.proof: S06: static (the three properties above, from the script text); dynamic A (whole self-test on a copy with tools/fixtures directories unwritable exits 0 and the whole-tree fingerprint is unchanged: it could not have written there); dynamic B and C (a leaking mutant is detected by each tripwire, so neither tripwire is vacuous). The real tree is never the subject of a write test: S06 copies it.

pinned_texts.readme_paragraph: The completeness guard also consults a **claim map**, the `FIXTURE_CLAIMS` array in the script: every subdirectory of `tools/fixtures/` is claimed by exactly one owning suite, as one `<subdirectory>|<suite file>` row, and a file below a claimed subdirectory, at any depth, is accounted for by that claim. The guard fails on an unclaimed subdirectory, on a doubly-claimed subdirectory, on a claim naming a suite file that does not exist, and on a claim naming a subdirectory that is not on disk. The self-test demonstrates those four cases itself, in a private scratch area that the scratch helper confines outside the repository, and prints one `OK   claim-map` line for each. A claim proves ownership, not execution: that the owning suite runs is proven by its own CI job (`tools/test_convergent_review.py` owns the `convergent_review` subdirectory and runs as the `convergent_review` job). A future suite that adds a fixture subdirectory registers its row in this same map; there is no second registry.

hazards: 1. SERIALIZATION. See design_notes.serialization. Consequence of the missing EXIT backstop (ah_premises_at_base[3]): any interruption (timeout, SIGINT) during the self-test can leave tools/skill.json swapped with the dangling-module fixture, which would make validate.sh C13 fail. S03 and S02 detect it; restore only by `git checkout <B> -- tools/skill.json` inside the attempt root. Prefix invariance (hazard 11) holds: the defect is before the separator and must NOT be fixed in 105.

2. SUBSHELL AND TRAP. scratch_dirs installs an EXIT trap that replaces the script's global one; every probe that calls it runs as a subshell function. _claim_map_case MUST be `name() ( ... )`; S06 enforces the header form. claim_map_check must not call scratch_dirs.

3. EMPTY ARRAYS. `"${FIXTURE_CLAIMS[@]}"` and the other arrays under `set -u` are only safe on bash >= 4.4; the script already requires bash 4 (declare -A) and CI uses ubuntu-latest. S05 case 7 empties the array and must still exit 1 with the expected message, not an unbound-variable error.

4. COUNT SEMANTICS. AT1 asserts accounted == total == the os.walk file count, so the accounted figure must include the files below claimed subdirectories and the total must be the any-depth count (find ! -type d matches os.walk's non-directory names; there are no symlinks to directories). Do not special-case 146.

5. AT3 reads the output for the NAME of the unclaimed subdirectory and the line `SELF-TEST FAILED`; AT2 matches the three OK lines as exact whole lines (`OK   claim-map   ` has three spaces on each side of claim-map). A trailing space or a different dash breaks them.

6. README. The paragraph is inside the last section of the file; AT4 slices on `### Fixture self-test` and `\n## `/`\n### ` and needs the substring `claim map`. C9 must not see an unresolvable backticked path: only existing paths are cited (tools/fixtures/, tools/test_convergent_review.py); the runtime_session paths appear ONLY in the script comment, never in a markdown file. C8 needs the 0.14.0 bump.

7. NIP SLOT. The runtime_session line is a COMMENT. A row for it would be a claim naming an absent subdirectory and would FAIL; the row can only be registered in the same change that first creates the directory (NIP-0003 feature 108, provisionally 115, per NIP lines 367-380; see pinned_interface.slot_rule). Creating the directory, stub, suite or row is out of scope (NIP-0003 phases 015/016).

8. EVIDENCE SHAPE (lesson from 103/104). Every .txt file has the invocation on line 1 and `EXIT:<code>` as the last line, the code read from the process, never from a pipeline (no `| tee`/`| grep` swallowing it). Do not capture AT or S output through a pipeline.
9. NO COUNTS. The new guard code contains no literal 79, 146, 67 or 12 (S04). The README and CHANGELOG pins mention 67 in prose; that is pinned documentation text, not guard code.
10. FIXTURES UNTOUCHED. AT3, S05 and S06 only write inside private copies. Nothing under tools/fixtures/ in the attempt root changes; S04 and S03 fail the attempt otherwise.

11. PREFIX INVARIANCE. The script before the completeness-guard separator is byte-identical to <A>. In particular the header comment, scratch helper, every probe and every note_covered row stay as they are; the new code follows the last probe.
12. AT1 TIMING. n is computed after the run; the self-test must not create files under tools/fixtures during the run (it does not, S06 proves it).
